clue.text: FBI class let loose with a Magnum? Shots fired!

definitions.note: plural shots set alight before drinking, as the definition describes

indicators.note: letting something loose sets it free to scatter, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A news flash about an FBI squad drawing a Magnum revolver, with a shout that shots have been fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let loose' tells you to rearrange the letters of FBI CLASS and A MAGNUM; 'with' just joins the two parts. The 'shots' are not gunfire but small drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Sambuca is an Italian aniseed liqueur often served as a small drink set alight, so these are shots that are literally on fire.

clue.text: Instead of sex, likely to get a spanking?

parts.note: for can mean in place of, as in swapping one thing for another
it is a euphemism for sex

explanation.surface: A kinky choice: a spanking rather than sex.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'in for it' means due a punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for being in trouble and due a punishment.

clue.text: Group of stars with City head for Derby's area

parts.note: and means together with
Rome is the Eternal City

indicators.note: head for says to take the opening letter of the word Derby

explanation.surface: A football piece: a group of star players from City heading for the Derby area.
explanation.walkthrough: Derby is an English city and the name of local football matches between rival clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: This constellation of the northern sky, named after a princess in Greek myth, is a pattern formed by a cluster of stars.

clue.text: Sacrifice one's motoring organisation company, but not love

parts.note: one's read as one is gives I and S
the AA is the Automobile Association, a British breakdown service

indicators.note: but not says the zero letter is taken away from the company abbreviation

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: Someone gives up a motoring club membership, though not out of love.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA (Automobile Association) is Britain's best-known roadside-rescue club. 'but not love' strips O from CO.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Abraham is ordered to offer up his son as an offering to God, so he is the biblical sacrifice.

clue.text: Cowardly way to cut down on fish preparation?

definitions.text: way to cut down on fish preparation?
definitions.meaning: to gut fewer fish when preparing them, read as two words

explanation.surface: A fishmonger's lazy shortcut is called spineless.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking guts means lacking courage, and the split phrase gut-less means gutting fewer fish.

clue.text: I will get involved in playing Ross at Lords?

definitions.note: plural nobles, matching the plural answer

indicators.note: getting involved in something means going into it, so the letter goes inside the rearranged letters
playing suggests the letters are messing about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone will join in when Ross plays cricket at Lord's.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is London's famous cricket ground, which is the picture; 'playing' rearranges ROSS AT around I.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a short informal word for aristocrats, and peers and lords are aristocrats.

clue.text: Eatery chain closes early after bars let out

indicators.note: after puts the shortened word for chain behind the rearranged letters
let out means freed to move, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, rearranged

indicators.note: closes early says the word ends before its last letter

parts.note: a series is a chain of events

explanation.surface: A restaurant chain shuts early once the bars empty out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let out' rearranges BARS to BRAS; 'closes early' takes the last letter from SERIES.
explanation.definitionFit: This French word names a casual restaurant, a place to eat.

clue.text: See-through top from Chanel put on king

indicators.note: put on says the letter sits above the king in the down answer
the top of a word is its opening letter in a down clue

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's king

explanation.surface: A sheer top from Chanel is put on a king.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'put on' means placed above: C goes on top of LEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Transparent glass or water lets you see straight through it.

clue.text: Stones' finale ends set with a rocky Satisfaction

indicators.note: the finale of a word is its last letter
rocky means unsteady, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: The Rolling Stones end a set with a rocking version of their hit (I Can't Get No) Satisfaction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocky' rearranges ENDS SET and A after the S; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being full or having had enough brings contentment, which is a kind of satisfaction.

clue.text: Joyful shout after flipping benefit comes in

indicators.note: comes in says the flipped piece enters the word for shout

parts.note: to rant is to shout angrily

indicators.note: flipping turns the word for benefit over, so it is read backwards

parts.note: aid is help or benefit

explanation.surface: Someone gives a happy shout once a benefit payment finally arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' reverses the word for benefit and 'comes in' places it inside the shout; 'after' is only a link, and 'Joyful' at the start is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A joyful person is said to be glowing with happiness, which is the figurative sense of this word.

clue.text: Eureka is what a sexually-active person might say

definitions.meaning: the cry of discovery, meaning I have found it

definitions.text: what a sexually-active person might say
definitions.meaning: a boast that one is having sex, 'it' being slang for sex

explanation.surface: A cheeky definition of a famous cry set against a bawdy boast.
explanation.definitionFit: Archimedes' cry of discovery is translated as a claim to have found something, and 'it' is slang for sex, so the same words serve as a boast.

clue.text: Shift clothes to store for Dolly?

indicators.note: to shift something is to move it around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is told to move their clothes into storage, perhaps for Dolly Parton's wardrobe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shift' tells you to rearrange CLOTHES TO. Dolly looks like Dolly Parton, but a dolly is a tool (a riveting tool or a wheeled platform), hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolly is an example of a workman's implement, and this box is where implements are kept.

clue.text: Scrap that woman had with royal at its centre

indicators.note: at its centre puts the letter for royal in the middle of the word for that woman had

parts.note: she'd is short for she had

explanation.surface: Gossip about a woman who had a quarrel with a member of the royal family.
explanation.walkthrough: SHE'D (she had) loses its apostrophe and takes R in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean a tiny fragment or piece, as in not a scrap of evidence.

clue.text: Soaks run dry, after knocking it back

parts.note: to flee is to run away

indicators.note: knocking it back says the word for dry is put back to front

parts.note: sec is the French wine term for dry

explanation.surface: Drinkers drain their glasses, knocking the drink back until it runs dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soaks' looks like drunks, but it is a verb meaning overcharges. 'knocking it back' reverses SEC, the wine word for dry, to give CES.
explanation.definitionFit: To soak someone is slang for charging them too much, a synonym for swindling or ripping them off.

clue.text: Celebration moves female with first signs of pregnancy?

parts.note: first is written 1st, read with the 1 as the letter I
a pregnant woman's bump shows she is expecting

explanation.surface: A woman celebrates her first signs of being pregnant.
explanation.walkthrough: 1ST for 'first' reads as IST when the figure 1 is taken as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Knocking knuckles together is a gesture people make when celebrating a success.

clue.text: Compel May's lot to prepare for a future fight?

parts.note: Theresa May led the Conservatives, informally the Cons
a boxer or soldier will train before a fight

explanation.surface: Pressure on Theresa May's party to get ready for a coming battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Theresa May was a Conservative British Prime Minister, so her party is the Cons.
explanation.definitionFit: To force someone to act is a synonym of oblige or force.

clue.text: Mostly break back with police unit or the army?

indicators.note: back says the shortened word is read in reverse
mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a rest is a break
the vice squad is a police unit dealing with vice

explanation.surface: Someone on a short break returns to choose between the police and the army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' cuts REST to RES and 'back' turns it into SER; then add VICE.
explanation.definitionFit: The armed forces are known collectively as the services, so the army is an example of one, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Hoskins is on time? You will be unprepared!

parts.note: Hoskins is the setter, so the setter is gives I'm
prompt means on time
U is text-speak for you

explanation.surface: The setter boasts of punctuality while warning the solver they will be caught off guard.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's name stands for I'M, a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: An off-the-cuff speech is given without rehearsal, so it is unrehearsed or improvised.

clue.text: Had a quick look at can's end drunkenly

indicators.note: something done drunkenly is all over the place, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drinker squints blearily at the bottom of a can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunkenly' says to rearrange the letters of CAN'S END.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan a page is to skim it, giving it a quick look rather than careful study.

clue.text: Comic supporting act: the Queen and the Queen Mum?

indicators.note: supporting means holding up from below, so the word for comic sits under the word for act

parts.note: to do is to act
a wag is a joker or comic
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A comedian is warm-up act for both the Queen and the Queen Mother.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supporting' puts WAG below DO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Queen Mother was the widow of a king, the classic example of a titled widow.

clue.text: Using sound waves, measures treeless flatlands

indicators.note: sound waves carry speech, so the clue asks for a word that is heard like the one for measures

parts.note: steps are measures, as in taking steps to deal with something

explanation.surface: A scientist uses sonar to survey bare plains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Using sound waves' is the signal: the answer is said like STEPS.
explanation.definitionFit: The great grassy plains of Russia and Central Asia have very few trees.

clue.text: Old singer's lust for one with a knack for gyration

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining singer to the wordplay

parts.note: lust is one example of a deadly sin

indicators.note: gyration means turning round, so the word for knack is reversed

parts.note: an art is a knack or skill

explanation.surface: A crooner known for lust and a gift for swivelling his hips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for gyration' reverses ART to TRA; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank, the twentieth-century crooner, was a famous American vocalist of the past.

clue.text: Can cleaner offer earl the foremost of treatments?

parts.note: a bid is an offer

indicators.note: the foremost of says to take the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Could a cleaner propose to an earl the best of her treatments?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' is not the verb but slang for a toilet, so the 'can cleaner' is a bathroom fixture for washing.
explanation.definitionFit: Can is slang for toilet, and this low basin beside it is used for washing oneself.

clue.text: Academic cut by heartless yobs is a sucker!

indicators.note: cut by says the academic is split open by the outer letters

parts.note: a don is a university lecturer

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letters are removed, leaving the outer pair

explanation.surface: A lecturer is slashed by thugs, and is a mug for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a sucker' looks like a dupe, but it is a vacuum cleaner brand.
explanation.definitionFit: The brand of vacuum cleaner works by suction, so is jokingly something that sucks.

clue.text: Prolonged blasts of flatus repelled male degenerates

parts.note: flatus is gas from the gut, also called wind

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so the word for degenerates is read backwards

parts.note: to rot is to degenerate

explanation.surface: A schoolboy tale of a man who fends off rotters with long bursts of gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repelled' turns back the word for degenerates, giving STOR, and the abbreviation for male follows; 'of' is a link. 'Prolonged blasts of flatus' wants to be one definition, but flatus is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A gale or tempest is a long period of strong gusts, matching prolonged blasts.

clue.text: Workers that could be described as Polish!

definitions.text: that could be described as Polish!
definitions.meaning: a pole, so it is pole-ish

explanation.surface: Employees who could be called Polish, a joke on nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: Employees are collectively the workforce, and a stick or rod is like a pole, so Pole-ish.

clue.text: Middle digits dimwits partly raised

indicators.note: raised says the hidden letters are read backwards
partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Fools half-raise their fingers.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'raised' means read upwards, i.e. backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the centre of something is being in the thick of it.

clue.text: Government problem about limiting smack and horse

indicators.note: limiting means enclosing, so the reversed letters hold the word for smack
about says the letters for government and problem are turned round

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
to tan someone's hide is to smack them

explanation.surface: A political story of a government struggling with heroin and horse, both slang for drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns G plus the word for problem round to MUSG, and 'limiting' wraps it round the word for smack. Smack and horse both look like drug slang, but only horse is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a breed of wild horse of the American West.

clue.text: Caught short? Leader must go!

indicators.note: the leader must go says the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: strapped for cash means short of money

explanation.surface: A political leader caught out is told to resign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught short' reads as one phrase but splits: 'Caught' is the definition, and 'short' gives STRAPPED, whose first letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal or person who is caught is held in a snare and cannot escape.

clue.text: Crack surgeon's first 'safe and natural' boobs

indicators.note: first says to take the opening letter of the word for surgeon
boobs are blunders, so the words are botched into a new order

explanation.surface: A cosmetic surgeon's opening pitch for breast implants that look safe and natural.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boobs' looks like the anatomy but is the verb to blunder, telling you to rearrange SAFE AND NATURAL after S.
explanation.definitionFit: The Californian geological fault is a long fissure in the earth's crust, a crack on a huge scale.
